parts.text:
Curve-type notation for vertical electrical sounding (VES): take the layer resistivities in depth order. For each group of three consecutive layers (layers 1-2-3, then 2-3-4, and so on), write one letter: A if r1 < r2 < r3; Q if r1 > r2 > r3; H if r1 > r2 < r3; K if r1 < r2 > r3. A curve with N layers gets N-2 letters, in depth order (for example, a 4-layer curve gets 2 letters, such as HA). If all the letters are the same, the curve may also be written as that single letter (AAA may be written A).

Station T-30, survey area T. Interpreted layer model:

Layer | Resistivity (ohm-m) | Thickness (m) | Depth to base (m)
----- | ------------------- | ------------- | -----------------
1 | 74.2 | 15.31 | 15.31
2 | 27.3 | 18.79 | 34.10
3 | 76.3 | 5.06 | 39.16
4 | 96.3 | 4.07 | 43.23
5 | 138.1 | - | -

What is the curve type of this station? Give a short answer, then end with one JSON line exactly like this:
{"curve_type": "<letters>"}

To determine the curve-type notation for the given vertical electrical sounding (VES) data, we analyze the resistivities of the layers in groups of three consecutive layers.

The resistivities are:
$\rho_1 = 74.2$ $\Omega\text{-m}$
$\rho_2 = 27.3$ $\Omega\text{-m}$
$\rho_3 = 76.3$ $\Omega\text{-m}$
$\rho_4 = 96.3$ $\Omega\text{-m}$
$\rho_5 = 138.1$ $\Omega\text{-m}$

Now, we examine each group:
1.  **Layers 1-2-3**: $\rho_1=74.2, \rho_2=27.3, \rho_3=76.3$. Since $74.2 > 27.3 < 76.3$, the pattern is $\rho_1 > \rho_2 < \rho_3$, which corresponds to the letter **H**.
2.  **Layers 2-3-4**: $\rho_2=27.3, \rho_3=76.3, \rho_4=96.3$. Since $27.3 < 76.3 < 96.3$, the pattern is $\rho_2 < \rho_3 < \rho_4$, which corresponds to the letter **A**.
3.  **Layers 3-4-5**: $\rho_3=76.3, \rho_4=96.3, \rho_5=138.1$. Since $76.3 < 96.3 < 138.1$, the pattern is $\rho_3 < \rho_4 < \rho_5$, which corresponds to the letter **A**.

Combining these letters in depth order, we get HAA.

{"curve_type": "HAA"}
